reason: The filtering capsules are shaped to surround the capillary tufts, making them a clear starting point for kidney filtration.
expectation: The tufts and capsules will form a filtering structure with a fluid outlet.

effect: The filtering units collect useful substances as well as wastes, so a recovery route is needed.
reaction: The reminder that filtration alone would lose useful substances clarifies the next task.
reason: Transport proteins in the tubule walls should provide a basis for reclaiming filtered substances.
expectation: The tubules will gain transport machinery for recovering glucose, salts and water.

effect: The recovery tubules now have selective transport machinery; they can be connected to the filtering units.
reaction: The separate positions of the pump and carrier make the recovery route clearer.
reason: The capsule outlets lead toward tubules, so joining these structures should connect filtration to recovery.
expectation: The filtered fluid will pass from the capsules into the recovery tubules.

effect: The filtering and recovery structures now form nephrons; they still need blood supply and drainage connections.
reaction: The nephron label ties the assembled parts to the kidney's working unit.
reason: The kidney blood-vessel branches should supply the filters and provide capillaries alongside the recovery tubules.
expectation: The working units will connect to blood vessels for filtration and return of recovered substances.

effect: The nephron units now have blood supply and vessels around the recovery tubules; the collecting and drainage route remains to be built.
reaction: The continuous vessel route makes the connection between filtration and recovery clearer.
reason: The collecting ducts merge toward the kidney drainage funnels, so these are a natural pair to connect.
expectation: The ducts will lead into the kidney's drainage funnels.

effect: The collecting ducts now lead into a renal pelvis with an open ureter outlet.
reaction: The drainage route is taking shape.
reason: The kidney units need a collecting route for fluid remaining after recovery.
expectation: The recovery tubules will connect to the collecting ducts, completing the kidney's internal fluid route.

effect: The kidneys now connect filtering, recovery and collecting routes while keeping blood separate from tubular fluid.
reaction: The parallel routes clarify where reclaimed material and remaining fluid go.
reason: The ureters connect the kidneys' drainage funnels to the bladder.
expectation: The kidneys will gain tubes carrying urine toward the bladder.
